papers.title: Index and Robustness of Mixed Equilibria: An Algebraic Approach
papers.abstract: We present two results regarding the relation of the index of equilibria and the index of fixed points, and the index of equilibria and payoff-robustness: any integer can be the index of an isolated completely mixed equilibrium of a finite game. In a particular class of isolated completely mixed equilibria, called monogenic, the index can be 0, +1 or -1 only. In this class non-zero index is equivalent to payoff-robustness. We also discuss extensions of the method of computation to extensive-form games, and cases where the equilibria might be located on the boundary of the strategy set. These results follow from a new method of computing indices of equilibria, which we also develop in this paper, that is based on algebraic properties of the system of polynomials describing completely mixed equilibria.

papers.title: Tate and Artin--Tate Motivic Tensor-Triangular Geometry
papers.abstract: We compute the Balmer spectra of geometric Tate and Artin--Tate motives with $\mathbb{F}_p$-coefficients over any field whose characteristic differs from $p$. For Tate motives, we find the bigraded comparison map to be a homeomorphism to the homogeneous spectrum of the motivic cohomology of the base field. For Artin--Tate motives, we describe the spectrum as a gluing of the spectrum of Artin motives computed by Balmer--Gallauer with the punctured Tate spectrum. We determine all specialisations between these pieces and the resulting topology. Under the hypothesis that the spectrum of rational Tate motives is a singleton, we also compute the integral Tate spectrum after inverting the exponential characteristic of the base field. As a consequence of our results, we identify the punctured Tate spectrum as an open subspace of the spectrum of the category of geometric Voevodsky motives, and draw some conclusions concerning the latter. Finally, we include an appendix where we define generalised periodicity in the context of tensor-triangular geometry, and explore its applications in motivic settings.

papers.title: Integral Hodge structures and atoms of fourfolds
papers.abstract: Following the recent work by OpenAI on the irrationality of very general cubic fourfolds in Hassett divisors, we prove some compatibility of Iritani's blow-up formula with the classical blow-up decomposition of integral Hodge structures. As a consequence, we express OpenAI's birational invariant in terms of the theory of atoms developped by Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu. We also show that, for every smooth complex rational cubic fourfold, the primitive cohomology is isometric as an integral Hodge structure to the twisted middle cohomology of a K3 surface and we prove irrationality of the very general Verra fourfold.

papers.title: Truncated Grassmannians: polytopes, representations, and Cauchy formulas
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to develop algebraic and combinatorial techniques for studying the geometric properties of truncated Grassmannians, a class of algebraic varieties obtained via certain projections of classical Grassmannians within their Pl\"ucker embeddings. We introduce a class of cyclic representations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of the general linear Lie algebra, which are proved to serve as duals of the homogeneous components of coordinate rings of truncated Grassmannians. We prove that the characters of these representations are computed via truncated Cauchy formulas and establish a connection with coordinate rings of complete collineations. We also construct monomial bases of these representations in terms of certain generalized chain polytopes and use the RSK correspondence to establish connections with Cauchy-type formulas and with Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns.

papers.title: Uniformization of compact K\"ahler Threefolds of Zero Kodaira Dimension
papers.abstract: Given two smooth compact K\"ahler threefolds $X$ and $Y$ whose universal covers are biholomorphic, we show that $\kappa(X) = 0$ if and only if $\kappa(Y) =0$.

papers.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$
papers.abstract: Bryan, Oberdieck, Pandharipande and Yin predicted the number of hyperelliptic curves on general abelian surfaces under a transversality condition. Some of the numbers have already been confirmed. In this paper we construct singular hyperelliptic curves on $(1,d)$ polarised abelian surfaces for $d\leq 15$ confirming a few predicted numbers, namely of (geometric) genus $g=d$ and of geometric genus $k+3$ on $(1,2k)$ and $(1,2k+1)$ polarised surfaces. Moreover, we have found that all genus 7 hyperelliptic curves on general $(1,8)$ polarised surfaces are double coverings of curves locally embedded into $(1,4)$ polarised surfaces. More interestingly, there is a unique genus 9 hyperelliptic curve (up to translation) locally embedded into a general $(1,12)$ polarised surface and it is a Klein covering of a curve locally embedded into a $(1,3)$ polarised surface.

papers.title: Rational curves of submaximal quantum index
papers.abstract: On a complex toric surface, oriented real rational curves tangent to the toric boundary at real points are distinguished by their value of quantum index. Using variants of usual Welschinger multiplicities, G. Mikhalkin defined enumerative invariants $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ that are provided by a signed count of oriented real rational curves with given quantum index $\kappa$ and fixed tangency points on the boundary of the positive quadrant (the tangency orders being encoded by $\tilde{\Delta}$). We prove that, for most toric surfaces and tangency orders, the invariant $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ is zero in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $\kappa$. This is done by enumerating tropical curves with Block--G\"ottsche multiplicities. Additionally, we prove that, in many situations, the lower bound, given by the absolute value $|W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}|$ of $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$, for the number of oriented real rational curves is not sharp close to the tropical limit in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $\kappa$.

papers.title: An atomic approach to Shokurov's conic-bundle conjecture
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply a weaker version of Hodge atoms to show that a standard conic bundle over a smooth complex projective rational surface $S$ is irrational if $|2K_S+\Delta|\ne\emptyset$, where $\Delta$ is the discriminant divisor. This proves Shokurov's conjecture on rationality of conic bundle threefolds. As an application, we deduce precisely which nodal quartic double solids are rational.

papers.title: Odd-Degree Rigidity and a Numerical Characterization of Complete Flag Varieties
papers.abstract: Let $F=G/B$ be the complete flag variety of a connected semisimple complex linear algebraic group. We prove that if a smooth Fano variety $X$ has the same dimension and Picard number as $F$, then the existence of a continuous map $X\to F$ of odd topological degree implies $X$ is isomorphic to $F$. In particular, a smooth Fano variety homotopy equivalent to $F$ is isomorphic to $F$. The algebraic input is a numerical characterization of complete flags: a positive-dimensional smooth Fano variety $X$ is a complete flag variety if and only if its pseudoindex $\iota_X$ is at least two and ${\rm ker}({\rm Sym}^2N^1(X)_{\mathbb R}\to N^2(X)_{\mathbb R})$ contains a positive-definite quadratic form. The pseudoindex condition can equivalently be replaced by the divisibility of $-K_X$ by two in ${\rm Pic}(X)$. The key observation is that a single definite quadratic relation excludes surfaces in every fiber of any elementary contraction; standard contraction theorems then yield smooth ${\mathbb P}^1$-fibrations and the characterization of complete flags applies. For the odd-degree theorem, Poincar\'e duality and a mod-two Wu-class argument show that the anticanonical class is divisible by two; comparison of the integral coroot lattices then identifies the flag. Most proofs were developed through extensive discussions with OpenAI's ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6), based on mathematical directions supplied by the author and arguments suggested by ChatGPT; see the AI Disclosure.

papers.title: Semipositivity and complete subvarieties of projectivised strata of holomorphic differentials
papers.abstract: We show that if the projectivised stratum $\mathbb{P}{H}_g(\mu)$ associated to a partition $\mu=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ of $2g-2$ contains a complete curve, then \[ \kappa_\mu:=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{m_i(m_i+2)}{m_i+1}>12. \] The weak inequality follows from semipositivity applied to a quotient of the Hodge bundle, while equality is excluded using the second Fujita decomposition and the geometry of fibred surfaces with maximal unitary rank. Consequently, no projectivised holomorphic stratum in genus $g\leq5$ contains a positive-dimensional complete subvariety. In genus $g=6$ the same conclusion holds for \[ (10),\ (9,1),\ (8,2),\ (8,1,1),\ (7,3),\ (6,4),\ (5,5). \]

papers.title: Disconnectedness of stability manifolds and their geometric loci, and separation of braid orbits of semiorthogonal decompositions
papers.abstract: This paper proves that the Bridgeland stability manifold $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ has infinitely many connected components for general quintic threefolds, other general complete intersection Calabi--Yau threefolds, certain odd-dimensional Calabi--Yau varieties, and certain rational weak Fano varieties. Moreover, we show that the geometric locus $\mathrm{Stab}^{\mathrm{geo}}(X)$ meets distinct connected components of $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ for general quintic threefolds and their products with varieties with finite Albanese morphisms, which gives examples in any dimension at least three. For the weak Fano examples, we also construct semiorthogonal decompositions in infinitely many braid group orbits. The proof is an extension of Nordskova's argument to families, using semilinear autoequivalences and absolute Galois actions on geometric generic fibers to permute mutually orthogonal spherical objects. Then, we specialize the separation to closed fibers. In our examples, the spherical objects are constructed from rigid rational curves or spinor bundles on quadrics.

papers.title: Tropicalization and Polyhedral Completions of Weyl Algebras
papers.abstract: We construct weighted and polyhedral completions of the Weyl algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field and organize them into a structure sheaf on a polyhedral $G$-site. For discretely valued fields, we prove two-sided flatness for $\Gamma$-rational polyhedral completions, yielding exact base change for finitely generated $D$-modules. For compact integral polyhedra, we also construct finite-type integral models whose special fibers are toric face rings and describe the reduction of Gauss points in terms of toric strata.

papers.title: Extended Tropical Characteristic Fibers and Slopes of Binomial D-Modules
papers.abstract: For a holonomic $D$-module, we consider the extended tropicalization of the reduced $L$-characteristic fiber along the family $L_s=F+(s-1)V_Y$. For $A$-hypergeometric systems, this tropical fiber determines the complete $(A,L)$-umbrella and hence recovers the classical slopes. We extend this result to holonomic binomial $D$-modules, for which the tropical jump parameters are exactly the classical slopes at the origin. As an application, a holonomic binomial $D$-module is regular holonomic if and only if there are no tropical jumps along any coordinate subspace.

papers.title: Relative Du Bois complexes over higher dimensional bases
papers.abstract: We extend the notion of the right relative Du Bois complex to a smooth base of arbitrary dimension. We further show that this complex satisfies base change in the sense of Kov\'acs--Taji, for flat families with strict higher Du Bois fibers, extending the result by Ning over a smooth curve.

papers.title: Deformations of Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms
papers.abstract: Recent work of Brantner and Taelman shows that derived deformation theory and period maps can recover strong mixed-characteristic lifting results. In this paper, we develop a prismatic version of this method for Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms, constructing compatible deformations over $A/I^n$ for every $n$ under suitable hypotheses. We also apply our method to $F$-split Calabi--Yau varieties over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. In particular, we consider an $F$-split smooth proper variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$, with $H^{d-1}(X,O_X)=0$ and trivial canonical bundle. We show that $X$ admits a lift to $W_3(k)$.

papers.title: $K$-tropical curves, Riemann-Roch and Serre duality
papers.abstract: We endow a tropical curve with the structure of a ringed space and establish analogues of Riemann-Roch and Serre duality for these ringed spaces. As a corollary, we give a cohomological proof of the tropical Riemann-Roch theorem.

papers.title: A Tropical Viewpoint on the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg Conjecture
papers.abstract: We give a tropical perspective on the recent arguments announced by OpenAI for Nagata's conjecture and the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg conjecture. By degenerating to both the normal cone and a semistable model whose dual graph is a cycle, we replace sections on a surface by Laurent polynomials in two variables. In place of theta functions, tropical methods bound the exponents of these Laurent polynomials, and a lift of the tropical Abel--Jacobi class of the normal bundle controls the shape of the resulting exponent diagram. Combining these support bounds with interpolation on a torus proves the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg conjecture with its predicted threshold whenever the corresponding linear series contains an integral curve whose only singularity is an ordinary node that is not a basepoint.

papers.title: The metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4
papers.abstract: Recently, OpenAI announced a counterexample to the Zariski multiplicity conjecture in dimension 4. Here, we prove that the metric Zariski multiplicity conjecture is true in dimension 4. More precisely, let $f,g\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ be germs of reduced holomorphic functions, and let $\varphi\colon(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$ be a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism such that $\varphi(V(f))=V(g)$. We prove that if every irreducible component of the tangent cone of $V(f)$ at the origin has a singular locus of dimension at most two, then $V(f)$ and $V(g)$ have the same multiplicity at the origin. In particular, the multiplicity of complex analytic hypersurface singularities in $\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\leq 4$, is an embedded bi-Lipschitz invariant; the cases $n=2$ and $n=3$ were known. This extends a previous result of the author for tangent cones whose components have singular loci of dimension at most one. We also prove that two irreducible homogeneous hypersurfaces whose singular loci have dimension at most two, and which are mapped onto each other by a homeomorphism of $\mathbb{C}^n$ fixing the origin, have the same degree.

papers.title: Motivic invariants of birational hyper-K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that birational projective irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds have equivalent integral cohomological motives as commutative algebra objects in $\mathrm{SH}(\mathbb C)$. Consequently, their algebraic K-theory spectra are equivalent as $E_\infty$-algebras, and their integral graded K-theory rings are isomorphic.

papers.title: Grassmannians of absolute Banach-Colmez Spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce Grassmannians of absolute Banach--Colmez spaces and prove the $k$-Grassmannian is perfectoid if and only if the space has slope $< 1/k$. For $d=1$, this proves a conjecture of Hansen--Mann. The key ingredient is a Pl\"{u}cker morphism, which realizes the $k$-Grassmannian of a slope $d/n$ space as a Zariski closed subspace of the projectivization of a slope $kd/n$ space. We also introduce a general method to construct invariant elements in perfectoid Tate--Huber pairs, and use this to prove absolute Banach--Colmez spaces of slope $<1$ have perfectoid projectivizations. As applications, we establish vanishing bounds for Scholze's mod $p$ Jacquet--Langlands functor on parabolic inductions, and also prove its vanishing in the top degree on every infinite-dimensional non-supersingular irreducible representation.

papers.title: Abelianization and moment maps
papers.abstract: When $X_G=\mathbb{C}^n/\!/G$ is a GIT quotient of a vector space, replacing $G$ with a maximal torus $T \subset G$ produces a closely related toric variety $X_T:=\mathbb{C}^N/\!/T$, the \emph{Abelianization} of $X_G$. Abelian/non-Abelian correspondences connect structures on $X_G$ with structures on $X_T$. In this paper, we study the interaction between the toric moment map $\mu$ of $X_T$ and $X_G$, when $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$. We do this by looking at the restriction of $\mu$ to an intermediate space $Z/T \subset X_T$, where $Z/G=X_G$. We show that the generic fibres of this map are co-Lagrangians that project to Lagrangians on $X_G$. We completely describe the image in the case where $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(2,n)$, and show that in the general $\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$ case the image can be sliced so that each piece is determined by a finite set of points, related to matroid circuits.

papers.title: Weighted flip graphs from cyclic quantum mutations: pentagon inequalities and exponential separations
papers.abstract: Positive cyclic quantum mutations at a third root of unity induce an explicit weight on polygon flip graphs. We study the resulting discrepancy between minimum flip count and minimum accumulated normalization loss. Every pentagon three-to-two replacement strictly decreases weight, and in connected types $A_1$, $A_2$, and $A_3$ every minimum-weight path is a flip geodesic. In type $A_4$, however, a six-flip path has smaller weight than the unique five-flip geodesic. A compatible positive projective gluing construction amplifies this example to an exponential success-probability separation in every connected type $A_n$, $n\ge4$. We also give a quantitative perturbation bound preserving the separation. The low-rank minimality statement has an exhaustive finite certificate; the pentagon inequality and the all-rank construction are analytic. In the associated sequential postselection model, differences of path weights determine success-probability ratios independently of the input state. The comparison holds for separately normalized exact mutation steps.

papers.title: On Boundary State Screening via Solitons
papers.abstract: We present a coarse classification scheme for the boundary data of massive QFTs based on transitions of boundary states via soliton / kink profiles. Starting from the lattice of boundary states, we introduce the boundary screening group $\mathbb{B}$: the equivalence classes of boundary states which cannot be connected by such transitions. In string theory backgrounds which geometrically engineer an interacting QFT in the target space, $\mathbb{B}$ computes the worldsheet analog of the target space defect group $\mathbb{D}$. When $\mathbb{B}$ is non-zero, it provides a diagnostic for having a target space with non-normalizable modes. For interfaces between QFTs, similar considerations imply the existence of a non-trivial conserved charge associated with soliton absorption / transmission, which means that the interface cannot fully dissolve / disappear. Similar considerations hold for junctions of QFTs, which in the special case of string worldsheet CFTs translate to junctions of string theories. We illustrate these general considerations with a number of non-geometric 2D $\mathcal{N} = (2,2)$ Landau-Ginzburg models, as well as their natural lifts to 4D $\mathcal{N} = 1$ Wess-Zumino models.

papers.title: Integral Brauer--Manin Obstruction for Fermat Near Misses
papers.abstract: We study the integral Hasse principle for the affine surfaces given by $x^4+y^4-w^2=m^2$, where $m>1$ is odd and squarefree. We give a criterion to determine if there is an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction, which depends only on simple congruence conditions on the prime factors of $m$ modulo $8$. We use this to show that for $100\%$ of such surfaces there is no integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle for integral points.

papers.title: Iterated toric descent obstruction and homogeneous spaces over geometric global fields
papers.abstract: We study torsors under tori and groups of multiplicative type together with the obstruction they define to the existence of rational points in the setting of geometric global fields. Our methods give two new arithmetic applications: the iterated toric descent obstruction coincides with the toric decent obstruction and the toric obstruction is the only obstruction to the existence of rational points for homogeneous spaces of connected linear groups with either connected or abelian geometric stabilizers. These applications generalize some known results for classical global fields, due to Borovoi, Colliot-Th\'el\`ene, and Sansuc, while exhibiting novel behaviors.

papers.title: Numerical Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for rank-three matroids
papers.abstract: We prove the numerical Kawamata--Viehweg conjecture for every matroid of rank three: the Euler characteristic of the inverse of an integral big and nef line bundle class is nonnegative. The proof reduces the conjecture to an inequality for a stone game.

papers.title: Alcove walks, crystal structure and a Levi branching rule
papers.abstract: In the Borel case $P=B$, we endow Haines' set of maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks (arXiv:2405.17174) with a crystal structure. We construct a bijection with the LS-gallery model of Gaussent and Littelmann (arXiv:math/0307122) and prove that it intertwines the root operators. This answers a question raised by Haines. We also extend the Gaussent-Littelmann stratification to the parabolic setting, prove the Levi branching rule for LS galleries, and compare the resulting gallery model with Haines' maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks in the parabolic setting.

papers.title: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
papers.abstract: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. Our majorants and minorants have controlled spectral coefficients and explicit stability under Hausdorff perturbations, uniformly over families satisfying a common Minkowski content bound. We extend the construction to singular spaces arising from Riemannian submetries with basic mean curvature, and apply it to equidistribution on quaternionic Shimura varieties. Assuming the conjectural formalism of the specified motivic L-functions, including the motivic Riemann hypothesis, we develop effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimates for fixed sets and varying families with controlled boundary geometry and Hausdorff variation, and describe how additional symmetries improve the error exponents. The proofs combine classical analytic methods with new methods from differential geometry, analytic geometry, and Riemannian spectral analysis. Applications include an asymptotic formula for a motivic analogue of Atkin-Serre estimates and tubular estimates for Picard-rank jumps of K3 surfaces via their transcendental motives.

papers.title: Baker--Akhiezer sections from Higgs bundles and Landau levels in hyperbolic band theory
papers.abstract: As observed by Kienzle and the second author, rank-two $\mathcal{O}(3)$-twisted Higgs bundles on the projective line encode all hyperbolic crystals of genus two: the spectral curves are the unit cells, and the Hitchin fibers are the abelian Brillouin zones. In a uniform magnetic field of two flux quanta, the lowest Landau level is one-dimensional at every nonzero momentum, and, as found by Iengo and Li, its dimension jumps to two at the zero momentum. We identify the states of the lowest Landau level with the Baker--Akhiezer sections of the Higgs bundles, and their zeros, the vortices, with the Baker--Akhiezer divisors. A family of nonzero momenta limits to the zero momentum exactly when each of the two vortices approaches the image of the other under the spatial inversion, and the states of the jumped level are labeled by the directions of limiting. On the Higgs bundle side, the zero momentum is the point where the Hitchin fiber intersects the Hitchin section. Such a family of Higgs bundles limits to the Hitchin section, thereby crossing to a lower stratum of the \BB stratification, an example of the phenomenon investigated in terms of Baker--Akhiezer divisors by the first author with Figiel and Teschner.

papers.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, remixed
papers.abstract: For each endotrivial complex for a $p$-group arising from Bredon homology of a representation sphere, we construct $p$-local quasi-isomorphisms, called forerunners. These enable us to extend Balmer--Gallauer's results concerning the tensor-triangular geometry of permutation modules for elementary abelian $p$-groups to all $p$-groups. We construct an open cover of the Balmer spectrum under which all endotrivials are tt-line bundles, that is, every endotrivial is locally isomorphic to a shift of the tensor unit. We define a remixed permutation twisted cohomology ring for which the canonical comparison map from the Balmer spectrum to the homogeneous spectrum of the twisted cohomology ring is injective. If the twisted cohomology ring is Noetherian, the comparison map is an open immersion, and the open cover endows the Balmer spectrum with Dirac scheme structure. We prove Noetherianity holds for Dedekind groups and the dihedral group of order 8, and conjecture it holds for all $p$-groups.
